How to obtain per-file import tables for a rev at all. build_index's documented return dict is exactly {version, commit, files, symbols, unresolved} — no import tables, and referenced_by cannot substitute (a bare `import pkg.mod` binds a module, and there are no module records to carry the edge). result.notes:
Yes — the thing to invoke is named unambiguously: analyzer.affected.compute_affected(repo, old_rev, new_rev) -> AffectedReport, with the observation channel fixed ("the value returned by the surface callable"). All seven done_when items land on that one return value, so none of them is untestable-for-lack-of-a-surface and I would file no untestable-guarantee defect. The seeded-vs-authored ratification also pre-clears the one thing that would otherwise look like a spec contradiction (callers_unknowable absent from Row's seeded field list), so I would not file that either.

Plan: each guarantee gets a fixture git repo built in .harness/scratch/ via git init + two commits (git -c user.email=... to avoid identity config), then one test asserting the discriminating side and, where the guarantee names a boundary, a second asserting the other side. Rows indexed by path into a dict so ordering is never assumed. (1) import-added-at-top: two top-level functions, assert both rows category == moved and no row in {signature, body, decorators}. (2) body-only edit to a symbol with a real caller: assert category == body, callers == [], and the caller's own path absent from rows. (3) signature change: assert a caller record exists per call site, keyed by in_symbol. (4) delete a called symbol: assert row.error and report.has_error, plus a negative twin (delete an uncalled symbol -> error falsy) since the errors clause is an iff. (5)/(6) plant an unresolved site via star_import in an importer file; assert callers_unknowable truthy, and a control fixture with a clean importer set asserting it falsy — that pair is what makes "never a bare zero" discriminating. (7) same, with the importer reaching the symbol only through pkg/__init__.py re-export. The trigger catalog is what makes 5-7 authorable at all; without it I could not manufacture an unresolved site.

Hedging where the packet is thin: truthiness rather than identity for callers_unknowable; membership/loose field probing rather than exact equality for caller records if I cannot settle their access shape; fixtures placed at repo root with explicit __init__.py to minimise the dotted-path guess. Every hedge gets recorded in tester_report.md as a weakened assertion, not silently.
